newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan earnings fall but beat estimates.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan earnings fall but beat estimates.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. said Thursday its earnings fell 15 percent in the second quarter, hurt by a decline in trading revenue, but the results beat expectations on Wall Street.
J.P. Morgan, the nation's fifth-largest bank, said net income fell to $374 million, or $1.85 a share, in the quarter from $440 million, or $2.14 a share, a year earlier.
But analysts had forecast earnings of $1.75 a share on average, according to First Call, which tracks Wall Street estimates, and Morgan's stock rose $1.81 to $108.18 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Trading revenue fell to $477 million from $697 million in both the first quarter of 1997 and the year-earlier period. The weak trading results had been expected by analysts.

But the shortfall was partly offset by gains in investment banking revenue, which is a good sign for the future, analysts said. Investment banking revenue rose to $294 million from $210 million in the year-ago quarter and $226 million in the first quarter.
"Investment banking is a blockbuster," said George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison. "They're continuing to prove that they are up there with the best."

Salem said overall the earnings were a "pleasant surprise" and the investment banking gains were significant because that is an important part of Morgan's plans. The company is considered more of an investment bank than most of its commercial bank competitors.

Raphael Soifer at Brown Brothers Harriman said that in the second quarter, Morgan ranked 11th worldwide as a lead stock underwriter and was fifth in combined debt and equity underwriting in the United States.
He noted Morgan had a better-than-expected performance with $124 million in revenue from equity investments vs. $126 million a year ago.
J.P. Morgan said the revenues included net gains of $118 million, mostly related to the sale of equity investments in the communications and insurance industries.
